Title: 'Anneaux simpliciaux canoniques et modules stratifiés', dated July–August 1967. A bracketed remark says the development is formally independent of the theory of crystalline or stratifying sites.

The mathematics, in modern terms:
- Let X → S be smooth. For each n ≥ 0 take the (n+1)-fold fibre product X^{[n]} = X ×_S ... ×_S X, with the diagonal immersion X → X^{[n]}.
- Take the formal completion of X^{[n]} along the diagonal. As n varies these form a simplicial formal scheme over X: the formal Čech nerve of X/S, i.e. the infinitesimal groupoid. All its terms have the same underlying space as X.
- Their structure sheaves P^n are pro-objects of sheaves of rings on that space, i.e. objects of Pro(Ann(Esp(X))). Together they form a cosimplicial ring P^* (the 'Anneau cosimplicial') with P^0 = O_X. This is the ring of principal parts of infinite order with its Hopf-algebroid structure.
- Stratified modules are the descent data / comodules over this cosimplicial ring: P^1-linear isomorphisms p_1^*M ≅ p_0^*M satisfying the cocycle condition.
- The purpose is a purely algebraic, site-free setup for stratifications and infinitesimal (de Rham) cohomology. This prepares the Nov–Dec 1967 lectures on crystals.
